question: The Commission is proposing that various funds under shared management, including cohesion and agricultural funds, are brought together under national and regional partnership plans. This raises questions for federal Member States such as Belgium, where important powers relating to cohesion, agriculture and regional economic policy have been constitutionally assigned to the regions. Analyses by the European Parliament also highlight risks to territorial cohesion, multi-level governance and the role of regions. 1.

How will the Commission guarantee that the NRPP structure remains in line with the principles of subsidiarity and proportionality, in particular in federal Member States where powers in the areas of cohesion and agriculture have been constitutionally assigned to the regions, and what formal safeguards will it put in place for these competent regional governments?

Can the Commission approve a national and regional partnership plan if competent regional governments within a federal Member State formally object to the proposed distribution or governance of the funds?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (5.8.2026) 1. Member States are responsible for designing their National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPPs) and for setting up their governance arrangements in line with their administrative, institutional and legal framework.

As set out in Article 6 of the Commission’s proposal1, NRPPs must be prepared and implemented in partnership with regional, local, urban, rural authorities and stakeholders in accordance with the multi-level governance principle and a bottom-up approach. The proposal enables regional chapters as part of the NRPPs.

The Commission’s President proposed in November 2025 additional clarifications to reinforce the role of regions in the design, implementation and evaluation of the Plans, including safeguards to prevent significant decrease in allocations to transition and more developed regions (unless justified based on objective criteria). The governance model for the NRPPs can be built on the existing implementation structures.

2. After the Member State’s submission of a NRPP, the Commission will need to assess whether the Plan complies with all applicable requirements, notably Article 22 of the proposal, including how the partnership principle in the preparation and implementation of the Plan is respected, and compliance with the European code of conduct on partnership.
As part of its assessment, the Commission may make observations to Member States and request additional information.
